title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes. Grothendieck is building auxiliary algebraic groups attached to two elements ρ and σ, presumably of orders 3 and 2, the generators of (P)SL2(Z) behind the loop relations of genus-0 and genus-1 Teichmüller groupoids. That identification is an inference and is unsure.

Setting, from the previous page:
- G is a reductive group of GL2 type. SG = SL2, PG = G/G_m ≅ Aut_gr(SG).
- B'_0 = T_0·L_0 is a Borel-type 'ax+b' group. T_0 is a one-dimensional torus with det: T_0 ≅ G_m (like diag(t,1)). L_0 ≅ G_a is its unipotent radical, parametrized by ε_0(λ).
- T_ρ is a torus attached to ρ.
- N'_σ is (part of) the normalizer of a torus T_σ attached to σ. ε_σ: N'_σ → μ2 detects the non-identity component.
- M_{ρ,σ}[0] ⊂ B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ is cut out by det u = det b = ε' det a, with ε'^2 = 1.
- M_{ρ,σ}(0) is the slice u ∈ T_0, and M[0] = M(0)·L_0.
- 𝒯_{ρ,σ} = M[0]/L_0 ≅ M(0).

This page:
- (24) Since det: T_0 → G_m is an isomorphism, the u-coordinate is determined by b. So projection to T_ρ × N'_σ is a monomorphism, with image {(a,b) | (det a/det b)^2 = 1}.
- (25) The characters become χ = det b, ε_2 = ε_σ(b), and ε_3 = det a/det b, which equals its own inverse.
- (26) 𝒯°_{ρ,σ} is the kernel of (ε_2, ε_3). It equals {b ∈ T_σ, det a = det b} = T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ, the fibre product over det.
- (27) This gives the extension 1 → 𝒯° → 𝒯 → μ2×μ2 → 1.
- (28) There is a further extension 1 → ST_ρ × ST_σ → 𝒯° → G_m → 1, given by χ = det. Here ST_ρ and ST_σ are the determinant-one parts of T_ρ and T_σ (29).
- (30), margin: 𝒯 ≅ M(0) acts on L_0 through the character χ, by g·ε_0(λ) = ε_0(χ(g)λ). This is the torus acting on a root group.
- (31) M(0) acts on SG via M(0) → T_0 → PG ≅ Aut_gr(SG), conjugation by the torus T_0. The map T_0 → PG is mono because T_0 meets the centre trivially.
- Next page: M_{ρ,σ} := M(0) ⋉ SG, with an extension by 𝔊^+ ≅ SG. It also gives an embedding of M[0] that extends L_0 → SG compatibly with (30).

Purpose: to build an algebraic-group 'model' (a semidirect product of SL2 with a disconnected torus-like group with μ2×μ2 component group). Such a group can receive the structures entering the loop equations, plausibly a GT- or Galois-type action on SL2-type completions.
errors: No mathematical error found. The steps (24)-(31) are internally consistent.

Minor notation oddities. In (25), ε_3 is written both as det a/det b and det b/det a; these agree because the ratio squares to 1. The notation 𝒯_{ρ,σ} versus T_{ρ,σ} is used inconsistently across pages, which Grothendieck himself flags in a margin note on the previous page.
In (29), 'ΓT_ρ' is presumably T_ρ (or its group of points). The Γ may be a slip or a transcription artefact.

ideas.what: Identification of M(0) with a subgroup of T_ρ × N'_σ via det: T_0 ≅ G_m, and decomposition into the identity component 𝒯° = T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ with component group μ2×μ2.
ideas.modern_name: fibre product of tori over the determinant; component group of a disconnected diagonalizable group

ideas.what: Extension 1 → ST_ρ × ST_σ → 𝒯° → G_m → 1 via the determinant character.
Action of the torus-like group on SL2 through T_0 → PGL2 ≅ Aut(SL2) and on the root group L_0 via the character χ; semidirect product M_{ρ,σ} = M(0) ⋉ SG.
ideas.modern_name: semidirect product with SL2 via inner automorphisms of a torus; torus acting on root subgroup
ideas.where_published: general framework in SGA3; this specific group not published

missed.claim: The page is part of an unpublished construction of algebraic groups M_{ρ,σ} (SL2 extended by a disconnected torus with μ2×μ2 components) tailored to the loop equations of the Longue Marche continuation. The construction itself is routine. Its role, presumably as target or hull for Teichmüller/Galois-type data in an SL2 setting, is not documented in the literature as Grothendieck's.
missed.quote: On fait opérer M_{ρ,σ}(0) (≃ 𝒯_{ρ,σ}) sur SG, par M_{ρ,σ}(0) → T_0 → PG ≅ Aut_gr(SG)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of interest when read together with the surrounding pages, as evidence of how Grothendieck intended to linearize the loop equations via GL2/SL2-type groups. That relates to later work on SL2-type or unipotent/relative completions of mapping class groups (Hain and others). The page alone carries no new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine bookkeeping of tori, determinants and semidirect products inside a larger unpublished construction. Nothing on this page itself is a new result.
transcription_corrections: Margin note beside (24) reads 'car T_0 ≅ G_m via det' (T_0 →~ G_m with det under the arrow), as transcribed.
In (29), 'ΓT_ρ' / 'ΓT_σ' may be just T_ρ, T_σ (the Γ is uncertain in the image).
The braced left margin note carries the label (30): 'L'opération de 𝒯_{ρ,σ} ≃ M_{ρ,σ}(0) sur L_0 est donnée par (30) g(ε_0(λ)) = ε_0(μλ), où μ = χ(g)'.
In (31), the subscript 'gr' is under Aut(SG), i.e. Aut_gr(SG). The lower row reads T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, G, and G/G_m ≅ Aut(G).
Handwritten folio number at bottom left is 415.
